text:
maria gomez: Hey folks — our CI started failing this morning with 401s against the Redwood API. Jobs that previously worked are failing after the runner rehydrate. Anyone seen this?
ben: same here, saw ~200 failures in last 30m. Response body has "error": "invalid_scope" in some cases, and straight 401 in others.
samir: can you paste the failing curl and the exact response?
maria gomez: here's the curl we use in the job (token redacted):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_CI_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-3.1","input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
Response snippet: `{"error":{"message":"invalid_scope: missing inference:invoke","type":"auth_error"}}`
ben: that message is telling — looks like the token doesn't include the inference scope anymore. Did we rotate service account perms?
ci-bot: Automated action: rotated service account 'ci-runner@redwood' keys for project 'infra-pipelines' at 2026-02-27T22:11:03Z. Token lifetime set to 7d.
maria gomez: whoa — we got a rotation but our runners expect 30d tokens. That explains failures after ttl.
samir: @infra_team did we change the global service-account policy last week?
infra_team: we pushed a change to tighten default lifetimes for service accounts created after Feb 20. New default for ephemeral CI tokens is 7 days (security posture). We did announce in #announcements but it looks like not all teams saw it. sorry about the churn.
ben: ok, two problems then: 1) token lifetime shorter, 2) scopes seem different for rotated tokens. The rotation job may be creating tokens with least-privilege scopes but our runner's service account needs `inference:invoke` + `models:list` at minimum.
maria gomez: how can we quickly unblock prod CI?
samir: temp workaround: create a short-lived personal token with the required scopes and set it in the project's pipeline secret. Not ideal but unblocks. Better permanent fix: update the rotation job to request explicit scopes and/or create a dedicated bot with correct minimal scopes and longer TTL, or migrate to OIDC-based ephemeral tokens.
ben: repro steps I used locally: created a token via the portal with scopes `[inference:invoke, models:list]` and ran the curl — success. Then created the same token via the rotation script and got a token lacking `inference:invoke` — looks like the script omitted `--scopes` in the `redwood tokens create` call.
Samir: can you paste the rotation script snippet?
ben: snippet from infra repo:
```
# infra/scripts/rotate-ci-token.sh (excerpt)
redwood tokens create --service-account ci-runner --expiry 7d --output json > /tmp/new_token.json
# missing --scopes parameter here
cat /tmp/new_token.json | jq -r .token > /etc/ci/secret
```
ben: so it creates a token but default scope set by server side might be limited. We should change it to: `--scopes inference:invoke,models:list` and validate the token after creation.
infra_team: i'll open a PR to change the rotation script and add a validation check. Also proposing a flag in the script to optionally set `--lifetime 30d` for dedicated CI projects (must be approved by security).
maria gomez: for the immediate unblock I updated the pipeline secret to a manually created token with correct scopes and jobs passed. will revert to auto-rotation once infra fixes the script.
samir: other follow-ups: 1) add an alert when token rotation results in >5% auth errors for a job, 2) post an announcement about default lifetime change, 3) document recommended pattern for CI (recommended: dedicated service account `ci-runner`, explicit scopes `inference:invoke,models:list`, prefer OIDC->short-lived or HashiCorp Vault refresh if long TTL needed).
ben: note on least privilege — avoid giving `billing:read` or `admin:*` to CI tokens. Some teams accidentally included broad scopes to avoid breakage.
deploy-bot: Incident note: created support ticket #SUP-2026-014 for tracking CI auth regressions. Assigned to infra_team.
infra_team: PR created at https://intra.redwood/p/r/infra/rotate-ci-token/45 — adds `--scopes` and an immediate validation step (curl /v1/health with token). Will also add a migration script to retroactively re-issue tokens for impacted projects.
maria gomez: thanks. Can we also get an ETA on the migration script?
infra_team: aiming EOD UTC. If any team needs priority reissue ping me directly.
ben: once PR merges we should rotate tokens in a controlled rollout (canary pipelines then all). Add a rollback plan in case of scope regressions.
samir: filing a short postmortem and a runbook update for service account rotation. Key learnings: rotation scripts must be idempotent and explicitly set scopes; communicate lifetime policy changes; prefer OIDC for CI where possible.
maria gomez: resolved for now — using manual token until infra's rotation script and migration land. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
__notes: thread contains root and reply messages in chronological order. names are display names. includes bot messages and code snippets.
